narrative.overview:
wynn.tools is a craftsman's logbook — dense, purposeful, made by someone who actually uses the tools they're documenting. The visual language starts from worn copper resting on carbon steel: a dark, near-black ground with a very slight warm cast (hue 30, barely perceptible), crossed by copper-bronze accents that light up under interaction like metal in firelight. The system never decorates; it indexes.

The display font is condensed and heavy — Barlow Semi Condensed at high weight — because players read stat tables and item names fast. The logo and section labels use monospace to mark them as system output, not marketing. Body text is Figtree: clean, warm, readable without trying to be friendly. The overall density is deliberate: Wynncraft endgame players are used to parsing dense data UIs. White space is earned by content, not distributed by default.

What this system refuses: RPG fantasy aesthetics (parchment, medieval ornament, pixel art), crypto-era maximalism (neon halos, blurry hero gradients, hype copy), and generic SaaS calm (orbital glows, rounded-everything, feature-icon grids). This is built by players with 400 hours in-game — it should feel like it.
keyCharacteristics: Dark ground, copper light — near-black warm surfaces; copper accent is the only color that truly illuminates
Condensed display weight paired with humanist body — authority and legibility at different scales
Monospace for system labels — timestamps, counts, the logo itself: anything that reads as output
No decorative elements except Wynnic script — the only permitted ornament is the game's own glyph system, used as texture at very low opacity
Flat at rest, glow halos on state change — depth is not structural; it's thermal

rules.name: The One Ember Rule
rules.body: Forge Copper appears on ≤15% of any given screen. Its presence means something is interactive or selected. Using it as a decorative fill collapses the signal.

rules.name: The No-Pure-Black Rule
rules.body: #000 and #fff are forbidden. Every neutral is tinted toward hue 30 (chroma 0.005–0.009). The floor is Carbon Hearth; the ceiling is Off-White Steel.

rules.name: The Gold Quarantine Rule
rules.body: Ingot Gold is game-world only. It does not appear on buttons, links, focus rings, or any UI element.

rules.name: The Mono-for-System Rule
rules.body: Any text that reads as output from the system — counts, coordinates, section labels, the logo — uses Geist Mono. Prose uses Figtree. Headings use Barlow Semi Condensed. These roles don't cross.

rules.name: The No-Decorative-Type Rule
rules.body: Barlow Semi Condensed does not appear at low weights. It ships at 600 minimum, 700–800 preferred.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No element casts a shadow at rest. Shadows and glows are purely state responses — hover, focus, elevation.

rules.name: The No-Lift Rule
rules.body: transform: translateY(-Xpx) is forbidden on hover for panels and cards. Horizontal nudge (translateX(3px) on arrow icons) is the permitted exception.

dos: Do tint every neutral toward hue 30. oklch(14% 0.006 30) is the floor; oklch(92% 0.004 30) is the ceiling.
Do use Forge Copper only on interactive, selected, or focused elements.
Do use Geist Mono for anything that reads as system output: counts, coordinates, section labels, the logo.
Do use Barlow Semi Condensed at weight 600 minimum.
Do cap body line length at 65ch.
Do use backdrop-blur + bg/90–95% opacity for floating map panels.
Do transition colors and background at 0.12–0.15s ease-out.
Do reserve Wynnic script decoration for hero sections at ≤5% opacity.
Do use prefers-reduced-motion: reduce to kill all transitions and animations unconditionally.
Do put focus rings at 2px solid Forge Copper with 2px offset on every interactive element.
donts: Don't use #000 or #fff. Every surface is tinted.
Don't use Ingot Gold (--color-gold) on UI elements. It's game-world context only.
Don't use a border-left greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards, list items, or callouts.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient). Use Forge Copper solid.
Don't use Glassmorphism decoratively. Backdrop-blur is structural only.
Don't use the hero-metric template (big number, small label, gradient accent).
Don't build identical icon-heading-text card grids.
Don't add parchment textures, medieval ornament, pixel art fonts, or anything that says 'this is a game' instead of 'this is a tool.'
Don't use crypto/NFT visual language: neon on black, blurry hero gradients, vague hype copy, orbital glows.
Don't use generic SaaS landing patterns: feature-icon grids, 'Ship faster' headlines, three-card feature rows.
Don't apply transform: translateY(-Xpx) to cards on hover.
